_SUPERSEDED: LEGACY PATH as of 2026-08-05. Production is now src/alert-skill/watch-loop.ts -- a persistent process ticking every 15s, installed as the Scheduled Task 'SMH-Hermes-Watchdog' by scripts/install-autostart.ps1. RUN ONE WATCHDOG, NOT BOTH: this job and the loop both persist .state/environmental-watch.json, so running both pages the on-call twice and races the cooldowns. install-autostart.ps1 refuses to install the loop while this job is enabled. See docs/WATCHDOG.md.
_why_superseded: Hermes cron cannot tick faster than ~2 minutes, for three reasons no config can reach: parse_duration has no seconds unit ({'m':1,'h':60,'d':1440}); the ticker thread polls on a fixed 60s grid; and mark_job_run computes next_run_at from the job's COMPLETION time, so a tick lands its due time just past the next poll and fires on the one after. Measured over 547 executions in cron/executions.db: 120s x415 while configured 'every 1m', 360s x113 while configured 'every 5m'. End to end that made the wait for the next tick ~86% of the worst-case sensor-edge-to-phone latency (102.2s measured).
_comment: Reference config for wiring the environmental watchdog into Hermes Agent's cron. Not consumed by any code in this repo -- Hermes' own `hermes cron create` CLI / `/cron add` chat command is the actual mechanism. This documents the exact parameters to use.
_mode: no_agent script watchdog. The script IS the job: Hermes delivers its stdout verbatim and delivers NOTHING when stdout is empty. Costs zero LLM tokens per tick, so the cadence does not compete with interactive queries (an agent-session tick costs ~3 min of NPU). All alert/cooldown/recovery logic lives in check-environmental.js -- which since 2026-08-05 is a thin wrapper over the shared tick in src/alert-skill/tick.ts, so this path and the loop cannot drift. The Python wrapper only translates the ALERT/NO_ALERT contract into 'print or stay silent'.
_schedule_note: 'every 1m' is the fastest this mechanism accepts and it really fires every 120s -- see _why_superseded. There is no seconds unit; 'every 15s' does not parse.
name: Environmental watch
_install: 1. Copy ./environmental-watch.py to %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\scripts\ -- Hermes blocks any script path that resolves outside HERMES_HOME/scripts.
2. hermes cron create --schedule 'every 1m' --name 'Environmental watch' --script environmental-watch.py --no-agent --deliver telegram
3. Verify through the SCHEDULER, not a manual run -- see _verification below.
_why_python_not_bash: Do not port this wrapper back to .sh. Hermes picks the interpreter by file extension (hermes-agent/cron/scheduler.py): .sh/.bash go to shutil.which('bash'), everything else to Hermes' own Python. On this Windows ARM64 laptop `bash` resolves only to WSL launchers (C:\Windows\system32\bash.exe and the WindowsApps alias) and the default WSL distro is docker-desktop, which has no /bin/bash -- so every scheduled tick failed with 'WSL (9 - Relay) ERROR: CreateProcessCommon:640: execvpe(/bin/bash) failed'. Python is always present.
_verification: A manual `hermes cron run` is NOT sufficient and previously gave a false pass: it inherits the invoking shell's PATH (which may include Git Bash), while scheduled ticks run inside the long-lived gateway process, which does not. Always confirm via a real tick: check that jobs.json shows last_status 'ok' after next_run_at passes, and that cron/output/<job_id>/ has a fresh entry.
_deliver_note: With no_agent the `deliver` field is correct, because empty stdout means silence by construction. The warning in ../skills/environmental-watch/SKILL.md against `--deliver` applies to *agent-session* jobs, where the model narrates every run.
_env: The script does not inherit the environmental MCP server's env block from config.yaml, so it sets UNOQ_LOG_MAX_AGE_S=180 itself. UNOQ_LEAK_DISTANCE_MM (water-level leak threshold) is left commented out until the tray is calibrated; the leak trigger currently used on stage is event-based.
